newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope to visit Brazil next October.
newsitem.headline: Pope to visit Brazil next October.

text.p: Pope John Paul will visit Rio de Janeiro next October for a meeting with Roman Catholic families from around the world, the Vatican announced on Monday.
The trip could provide an opportunity for the 76-year-old Pontiff to visit communist Cuba following an invitation from President Fidel Castro during an historic audience at the Vatican last month.
The Pope's visit to Brazil on October 4 and 5, 1997 will be his fourth to the country, the most populous in Latin America.

Cardinal Alfonso Lopez Trujillo, chairman of the Pontifical Council for the Family, told a news conference that the Pope would meet families in Rio's Maracana stadium on October 5 and celebrate open-air mass the following day.
The Pope has made the "defence of the family" from the dangers he says are posed by modern society, including divorce, abortion and cohabitation outside marriage, one of the themes of his papacy.
The Church's "World Meeting with Families" in Rio will be the second, following a similar event in Rome in October 1994.
Lopez Trujillo made no reference to a Cuba visit, though Church sources say it would made sense for the Pope to travel to the Caribbean island on the same trip.
Cuba is the only Spanish-speaking country in Latin America which the Pope has not visited.
The Vatican and Castro said after last month's audience that no conditions had been attached to the visit and that both sides hoped it would take place in 1997.
The Pope is also scheduled next year to visit Prague, his native Poland and Paris.
